Speaker: The Wanderer

Speaker: (narration)

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: Easy. Stay down. Hands like ice, pulse like a rabbit's. We'll fix that later.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: Keep your voice low. We are not the only ones in these woods tonight.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: I don't know this place. I don't know my own name. ...Who are you?

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: A friend. That's all I can give you, and it's already more than is safe.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: Can you still fight, still draw on the Paths? Hold out your hand like you used to... never mind, just your hand.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: ...I feel them. All four, faintly. Like voices through a wall.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: Faint will do - it has to. Those torches on the ridge are looking for us.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: Tell me: which Path resonates the strongest within you?

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: That one, then. Hold on to it, and it will hold on to you.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: Behind me is the Forgotten Cave. Follow it all the way through to {town}. Someone there will be waiting for you.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: Hear that? They're close. I'll draw them off the other way. They know my face; let them chase it.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: So you go on alone. Don't thank me. Thank me when you're somewhere with a roof. Go!

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: ...Gone, toward the torches. I never even asked their name.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: The trees close up that way. The cave, then.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: No point getting lost twice in one day. Back to the cave.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: Whatever is waiting for me, it's through that cave.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: Torches that way, cave this way. I'll take the one that isn't looking for me.

Speaker: The Hollow Warden
Current line: ...Hm. Woken. For this. Another of the little scavengers, I suppose.

Speaker: The Hollow Warden
Current line: ...No. Not that. You smell familiar. Like old stone, and cold nights, in a house I used to keep.

Speaker: The Hollow Warden
Current line: The house does not open for just anyone. ...Show me.

Speaker: The Wanderer

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: Hm. Then we start with tea and pie and work up from there.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 0)

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 1)

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 1)

Speaker: Elder Maren

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 2)
Current line: And if you meet Wren in the Capital, tell her my pie is still the best thing in the kingdom. She'll argue. She'll be wrong.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 3)

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 3)

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 4)

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 4)

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (known early)

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (known early)

Speaker: Elder Maren

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (first)

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (first)

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (return)
Current line: The roads are waiting, dearie: the Gainlands, the Buffet, the D.N.A. and the Dump. One zone at a time.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (return)
Current line: You could still be anyone's spy. I have been wrong about people before. Once. In 1987.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (idle)
Current line: Still here, dearie? The roads won't walk themselves. Well. Some of them would, if {villain} let them.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (idle)
Current line: The pie on the sill is cooling, dearie. Unlike you, it knows when to wait.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (idle)
Current line: If you're looking for advice: eat something. If you're looking for more advice: eat something else.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (idle)
Current line: I've given you all the answers you need for now, dearie. Further questions require fieldwork.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (idle)
Current line: Mind the fountain, dearie. People throw wishes in it. Most of them are mine.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (idle)
Current line: Off you go, dearie; I'll be here. I'm dependable at a speed you can barely measure.

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
When it's heard: Talking to Gatekeeper Brannoch in Crosspath (capital offer)

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
When it's heard: Talking to Gatekeeper Brannoch in Crosspath (capital offer)

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
When it's heard: Talking to Gatekeeper Brannoch in Crosspath (capital offer)

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
When it's heard: Talking to Gatekeeper Brannoch in Crosspath (capital active)

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
When it's heard: Talking to Gatekeeper Brannoch in Crosspath (capital done)

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
When it's heard: Talking to Gatekeeper Brannoch in Crosspath (capital done)

Speaker: Sable

Speaker: The Store Room Ghosts

Speaker: The Store Room Ghosts
Current line: We'll go. The chapel belfry has a lovely draught and nobody has complained about it in centuries.

Speaker: The Store Room Ghosts
Current line: Tell Tilly the lantern's on the top shelf, still broken after ninety years of nightly checks. We were thorough, if poorly lit.

Speaker: The Store Room Ghosts
Current line: Ha! No refund, no entry. Come back with a better deck. Or a receipt. Ideally both.

Speaker: (narration)

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: That one is already back in the pen. It is sulking. It will get over it.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The vine bridge sways and creaks cheerfully. It is made of vines, ambition and a lot of compost.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The seed cracks. The soil heaves. Green shoots race into the air, twisting and knotting...

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: It has grown! You try to picture the spot without it. The druids look pleased with themselves.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: You climb the beanstalk, hand over hand. The leaves are big enough to sit on. Do not sit on them.

Current line: You crawl out through the old tunnel and push the rubble aside. The Outskirts again, and a long way from anybody's approved queue.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: You squeeze back down the collapsed shaft and follow the old tunnel in the dark.

Speaker: (narration)

Speaker: (narration)

Speaker: (narration)

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: You post a complaint. A hatch opens and a warm cup of tea is pushed out, still steaming. 'We value your concern,' says a note. You feel a little better.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: You post a complaint. 'Noted,' says the box, gently. You wait. That appears to have been the whole service.

Speaker: (narration)

Speaker: Wren

Speaker: Wren

Speaker: Wren
Current line: Three. He is afraid, you know. Not of you.

Speaker: Wren
Current line: Of everything that will not obey. A small, sad fear, for a man with so much gold.

Speaker: Wren
Current line: All four. I have the whole of him now. He is not a monster.

Speaker: Wren

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Current line: My crews run six hours a day... for ten years. Nobody's told them they can stop. Somebody ought to.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Current line: Three wheels... pull the brakes. And that big cable by the east wall... feeds the facade. Cut it.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: I used to measure people. Now I just look at them. A man walked past yesterday who was nine feet tall and I said 'good morning'.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: I am not myself. I am much better.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: Come in, come in. Bring any height.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: Queue management. There is no queue any more. I am standing here out of habit.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: Nobody has told me where else to stand. I keep almost asking permission to go for a walk.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: Still no queue. I am doing very well.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: Exit control. You may leave whenever you like. I am just standing here. It is a very open exit.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: Exit control. Goodbye. Come back. Goodbye.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: Exit control. This is an exit. It is also an entrance. It is, from every angle, a door.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: A door. A good door.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: Exit Interview Booth. Name? Reason for leaving?

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (intro) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: ...I was never going to read the answers. Please go and have a nice day.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
When it's heard: Talking to Capital guards and clerks (return) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: Have a nice day.

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
When it's heard: Talking to Nurse Hesper Dray (intro) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: Hesper Dray. Sit. Drink.

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
When it's heard: Talking to Nurse Hesper Dray (intro) (after the zone is freed)
Current line: Still unapproved. Nothing's approved any more. Best thing that ever happened to my tea.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Scene "maren after capture" (maren after capture), step 1
Current line: Sit down, dearie. Word came from the Capital this morning, by way of a pigeon who was very rude about it.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Scene "maren after capture" (maren after capture), step 2
Current line: Plume's men took a girl at the castle gate. The one who carried you out of the woods. {rescuer_full}.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Scene "maren after capture" (maren after capture), step 2
Current line: I knew that face the day you walked in here. Her father worked in my laboratory, once. I never trusted her for a minute.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Scene "maren after capture" (maren after capture), step 3
Current line: I have been wrong about people before. Once. In 1987. It seems I've gone and done it twice.

Speaker: The Wanderer
When it's heard: Scene "maren after capture" (maren after capture), step 4
Current line: Where did they take her?

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Scene "maren after capture" (maren after capture), step 5
Current line: Back where she came from, I expect. Somewhere with glass walls and no windows. That's a door I can't open. Not yet.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Scene "maren after capture" (maren after capture), step 5
Current line: Eat. You'll want your strength for when it opens.

Speaker: Wren
When it's heard: Scene "wren after capture" (wren after capture), step 1
Current line: We saw them take her at the gate. Four guards and a peacock with a speaking trumpet. We couldn't get close.

Speaker: Wren
When it's heard: Scene "wren after capture" (wren after capture), step 2
Current line: The Wrinkles are watching every door out of that castle. If they move her again, we'll know.

Speaker: Wren
When it's heard: Scene "wren after capture" (wren after capture), step 2
Current line: Her name goes in the true record. Whatever else happens.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The Model Falls

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: You hear the scale model split. The table cracks beneath it, and the sound travels through the castle walls.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: In the gallery a portrait slips off its hook and lands face-up. For the first time in ten years, nobody picks it up.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The Facade Falls

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: In {showcase}, a painted door falls flat. You see a citizen step through onto the street beyond.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Shopfronts topple. Hedges wilt into their own shapes. The loudspeakers cough once and go quiet.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Behind the facade: houses, lawns and people, all of them a bit crooked. A child paints the new sign at the gate: PATHORDIA.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The Rifts Close

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Across the Capital the rifts fold up like letters. In the Reek, the Sick Patch is a flower bed.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: In Grave Row, a family walks slowly to a quiet plot and stays. In the Transit Yards the wheels slow, and slow, and stop, and the crews lie in the sun.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: In the Hungry Quarter, somebody lights a stove.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The Wrinkles

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The Wrinkles climb up out of the Crease, blinking, into a light they had forgotten. Wren carries the true records under her arm. Nurse Hesper has brought the tea.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: You see Fig Sly among the people emerging from the Crease. He carries his stock with him.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The Paths Meet

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: And the Paths come home. Grandmaster Flex, the Grand Chef, Agnes Overdue and Archdruid Compostella meet in the plaza and look at one another for the first time in ten years.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: You watch the four Paths gather around their leaders, carrying what they have saved from the past ten years.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Nobody agrees on anything. It is the happiest sound the Capital has ever heard.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Together

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: {villain} demanded one way for everyone. It was never what made the kingdom strong.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: You see hands marked by iron, flour, ink and soil reach across the space between the four groups.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The point was never to be the same. The point was the argument. Different Paths, working together.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The New Decree

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: A new decree appears on the plaza wall of {pathordia}, in four different handwritings. It reads: DIFFERENT PATHS MAY MIX AGAIN.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: You read the changes beneath it: MAY crossed out for SHOULD, then WILL, IF THEY FEEL LIKE IT. Four hands have left their marks.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: THE END (OF THE BEGINNING)

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: A game about a kingdom that was strong because it was not the same.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: PLACEHOLDER CREDITS

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Design and direction: you

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Engine: Godot 4

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Art: Kenney, KayKit, game-icons.net and friends (see CREDITS.md)

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Music: synthesized in code

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: {villain}'s rule is over. The voices of the kingdom remain.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: For everyone who waited to be heard.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: For everyone learning to choose again.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The Paths will be back, in some other order.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Thank you for playing.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: You are back in {pathordia}. It is mostly the same streets, but it sounds quite different: people are shouting at each other cheerfully, in every direction.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Wren sits on the edge of the fountain with a ledger on her knee, writing the title of the first honest page: THE TRUE RECORD, VOLUME ONE.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The Capital is free. The postgame begins: decks of three or more Paths are now allowed.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
Current line: Breathe in. Hold. ...Feel that? That is a city with nowhere it has to be.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
Current line: Rollo's crews are lying in the sun. I told them rest is a rep. They believed me. Heart and mind, son. You used both.

Speaker: The Grand Chef
Current line: The sauce is gone from every stove in the kingdom. Real onions again. I have not wept so much since I was a girl.

Speaker: The Grand Chef
Current line: You did something worth signing, you know. Now sit. Eat. Eat a mess.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Current line: Thank you, dear. I have written it down, though that hardly seems enough.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Current line: I think I am going to cry. I have wanted to for a very long time.

Speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
Current line: Look at this crack in the marble. Something is growing out of it.

Speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
Current line: I am going to let it. It has earned the right. So have you, child.

Speaker: Primm
Current line: ...You do not even know, do you? Look at you. You have walked my castle for hours and you have not once asked why my portraits stop at eleven.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: ...What do you mean?

Speaker: Primm
Current line: I kept your face. I kept it for ten years, in the one gallery I never let anyone clean. It is the only face I could not improve.

Speaker: Primm
Current line: You are the Royal Asset. You are the boy who got out. You are {prince_full}, and you have been so very hard to find.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: ...That's not possible. I would remember.

Speaker: Primm
Current line: Your power has kept this kingdom lit for ten years. I have only been looking after it. Surely you can see that.

Speaker: Primm
Current line: Come. You may as well see it used properly.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: the Pathwork Throne

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The castle does not fall. It opens. Where the Model Room floor was, a stair of four colours winds down into the old heart of the Capital.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: At the bottom stands the Pathwork Throne: four seats grown into one, four colours woven as a single thread. It was never {villain}'s.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: You sit, and the Throne answers. It knows you.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Everything comes back at once: the lullaby, the glass, the throne room, the name. {prince_full}. And the Paths, all four, as they were always meant to be carried.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: {villain} Sees

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: {villain} sits among the pieces of his model. As the Paths settle, he sees the kingdom as it is, and not as his reflection.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Cracked streets. Real faces. A boy he kept in a cell.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Slowly, he understands how much he broke. The wells were good. The schools were good. He made one choice for everyone, and nobody will trust him with another.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Current line: File Complete

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Current line: Agnes Overdue floats up to the old transfer file, finds the heir clause and, with great ceremony, brings down her stamp: HEIR: ALIVE. FILE COMPLETE.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Current line: You see Maren make her way through the crowd. She stops in front of you, flour still on her sleeve.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Current line: '{prince},' she says. It is the first time anyone has said it aloud and meant it. 'Welcome home.'

Speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
Current line: Do not look so alarmed. The guard is very kind, and the workshop has a very nice window.

Speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
Current line: I am designing a water main. A real one: pipes, a pump and nothing clever. It is the first thing I have made in ten years that nobody had to agree to.

Speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
Current line: I am not permitted to speak of the Paths, or to touch one. I find that I do not miss it. I find that I miss the wells.

Speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
Current line: He is allowed visitors, one at a time, ten minutes, no mirrors. Those are the rules. I did not write them, and I find I do not mind them.

Speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
Current line: He designs good drains. The guard stays here while he works.

Speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
When it's heard: Scene "hob town funeral" (hob town funeral), step 1
Current line: Ah. You did it, then. The castle.

Speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
When it's heard: Scene "hob town funeral" (hob town funeral), step 1
Current line: Then I've two graves to finish properly, up in the city. Grave Row. Come by when you're ready. No rush. There never is, with me.

Speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
When it's heard: Scene "hob town after funeral" (hob town after funeral), step 1
Current line: Back again! Walked them all the way home, I did. Lovely evening for it.

Speaker: The Wanderer
When it's heard: Scene "hob town after funeral" (hob town after funeral), step 2
Current line: What are you writing?

Speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
When it's heard: Scene "hob town after funeral" (hob town after funeral), step 3
Current line: Appointments. Let's see. You... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Someone is walking down the imperial road in faded pastel regulation clothes, a bedroll over one shoulder. Brannoch has stopped writing in his notebook.

Speaker: Isla Brannoch
Current line: Hi, Dad. I know. I should have written.

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
Current line: Hm.

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
Current line: Eight years. Gate stayed open. Every night. In case.

Speaker: Isla Brannoch
Current line: They had us painting the same front door for eight years. Every time I asked to leave, the form came back "pending".

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
Current line: ...You've got your mother's curls. Still can't keep a ribbon in them.

Speaker: Isla Brannoch
Current line: And your nose. Mum always said that was the unlucky part.

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
Current line: Wrote you in the book. Every day. "Isla. Not yet."

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
Current line: Today it says "home".

Speaker: Isla Brannoch
Current line: You're the one who knocked the castle over? Dad says hi. Dad says a lot, actually. Thank you.

Speaker: Isla Brannoch
Current line: I keep walking to the gate and back. Nobody stops me. I keep expecting somebody to stop me.

Speaker: Isla Brannoch
Current line: Dad oiled the hinges this morning. It doesn't even lock. He just likes the sound of it opening now.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Grave Row, at dusk. At the end of the identical rows stand two new headstones, and they are not identical. Someone has carved them by hand: a crown, a harp, four colours in a ring.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Half the city has come. Nobody was told to. Wren holds the true record. Maren holds a pie she has forgotten about.

Speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
Current line: Ten years I've been digging these two. Slowly. I didn't want to finish before they could be visited properly.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Current line: Two forms, filed ten years ago, stamped by me. And a third, for a little boy, that I never had the heart to file.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Current line: I'm tearing that one up now, dear. With great pleasure.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: He used to say the Paths argued like family. She used to say that was the point.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: A warm wind comes up the row, out of season. Two figures stand by the headstones, the way people stand in a doorway when they are leaving and not sorry to.

Speaker: King Harmon Wayweaver
Current line: Look at you. You came home.

Speaker: Queen Concordia Wayweaver
Current line: Carry them gently, love. All four of them.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: She hums the first bars of the lullaby, and does not need to finish it. You know the rest.

Speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
Current line: Right then, Your Majesties. Mind the step. It's a long one, but it's downhill all the way.

Speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
Current line: And you, Agnes. I've had you down for this a very long time.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Current line: One more week, Hob. Prudence needs a proper handover, and somebody has to explain the new handbook to Mortimer.

Speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
Current line: Hm. Pencilled in. Heh.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: When you look again there are two headstones, a top hat bobbing away down the row, and a great deal of warm wind.

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
Current line: Hm. She's home.

Speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
Current line: Notebook's full of her name. Started a new one. First page says yours. Spelled right, this time.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: In the Capital's square, you watch the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands. Several people cry.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Above you, four banners share one crowded pole.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: At the crowd's edge, you see a hooded traveler smile, leaves still in their hair. There is always another path.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The Paths Unbound

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: With {villain} gone, the Paths are free to mix again. Your decks may now combine cards from ALL Paths, and the Alchemist's tri-Path crafting is open. What made the kingdom strong was never sameness.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: Decks may now use 3 or more Paths.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: The Alchemist's tri-Path crafting is unlocked (no tri-Path recipes exist yet).

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: {pathordia} is open to everyone: the facade is down, the rifts are sealed, and {villain} works under guard on wells and pipes, kept away from every Path.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (postgame)
Current line: {villain} is gone, and the Paths are shouting at each other in the street again. I have never been so glad to be annoyed.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (postgame)
Current line: The Capital is open to everyone now, and your decks may mix any Paths you like. Go and see what you can make of it, dearie. Then come home and eat.

Speaker: (UI)
Current line: {villain} has fallen and the Paths are free to mix. Build decks from three or four Paths at once, try the Alchemist's tri-Path crafting, test yourself in the Undercroft and visit the changed Capital.

Speaker: The Rescuer
When it's heard: Postgame: rescuer (after the zone is freed)
Current line: You came for me. Twice, if you count the woods. I'm counting the woods.

Speaker: The Rescuer
When it's heard: Postgame: rescuer (after the zone is freed)
Current line: Finish it, Tess. I'll be here. I've had a lot of practice waiting in this forest.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: The Lab is quiet. For the first time in ten years I can hear the trees from down there.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: Dad is in {town}, listening to Maren. She let him have one slice of pie. One. I've never seen him so frightened.
